# P09 correction: rc metadata, real migrations and pending owner policies

Source: [JSON](../../decisions/D121.json). This view is for people; agents use JSON through the Task API.

## Date

2026-10-06

## Status

accepted

## Context

Verified against scripts/schema-sets.json, scripts/manifest-check.py, composer.lock and JSON review B1/B5/B7. D119 had unsupported owner choices.

## Decision

Supersedes D119. Preserve D19 lockstep and first 1.0.0-rc.1, optional-to-install corex-full (required candidate deliverable). Candidate identities: 21 existing CoreX packages plus full; channel counts and public dependency set remain pending D123. Access has no AzGuard runtime requirement; legacy channel cannot settle its policy. Split implementation remains D19 until owner answers D122; deterministic archive export is local preparation, not approval of an alternative remote mechanism. Include every declared SchemaSet path under database/migrations/, including root, tenant, tenant-cloud and budget from scripts/schema-sets.json. Source internal requirements, including full, remain ^1.0@dev; exporter writes exact =1.0.0-rc.1 dependencies. No source version. Before candidate build P09.6 changes access-azguard extra.corex.stability from unreleased to stable and removes manifest UNRELEASED exception; this is BC enforcement metadata, not a declaration that the rc version is Composer-stable or that its channel is public. D17 blocking BC applies to every rc library including the bridge; full receives dependency/manifest compatibility checks and no vacuous PHP Roave pass. Public roots keep minimum-stability=stable with explicit root @RC allowance on each reachable internal rc package; no minimum-stability=dev workaround. Rector/Pint exclude all packages/products database/migrations trees while PHPStan includes owned directories. Publication remains separate owner grant. No split, access channel or hosted credentials authorization is inferred.

## Rationale

Resolve executable technical contradictions without exercising reserved owner decisions. Optional consumption differs from required export of the optional metapackage.
